Kassel, 1812: the Teller of Tales

Kassel, in the autumn of 1812. In the inn by the town gate a farmer's widow from Zwehrn, Dorothea Viehmann, sits by the fire and tells the old tales, word for word, the same every time; and two brothers, Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, write them down.
Kassel, in the autumn of 1812
Go to the Knallhütte inn, at the top of the market square.
Dorothea Viehmann is by the fire. Speak with her.
▶ "Tell me the first."
The landlord brings the brothers' notebook. Speak with him.

"The Grimm gentlemen left their notebook. Will you carry it to them? They live on the Marställer Platz, the house with the green door. They'll want every tale she tells you, mind, written down true. "
Carry the notebook to the Brothers Grimm's house.
Give the notebook to Jacob Grimm.

"Ah! Frau Viehmann's tales. Good. We are collecting every tale the people of Hesse still tell, before they are lost : just as they are told, not prettied up. Go and live them, one by one, and bring us something from each, so we know they are true. Wilhelm will write them fair."
Wilhelm Grimm has a quill for you.

"Take this quill, and keep it. And mind: in the tales, the good are rewarded and the wicked punished, and you must do what the good ones did: share your bread, keep your word, and be clever. Begin with the woodcutter's children. Their cottage is south-west, in the deep wood."
The manuscripts on the desks
Look at the manuscripts the brothers have collected.
Hard by a great forest dwelt a poor wood-cutter
Find the poor woodcutter at the edge of the great forest (south-west of Kassel).
"Hard times. A great dearth has fallen on the land, and I can no longer get even our daily bread. My wife says... no. I will not tell you what my wife says. Go in and see the children , if you will."
Go into the woodcutter's cottage.
The children's straw bed
It is night. Lie by the children's straw bed and listen.
Gretel is weeping bitterly. Speak with her.
"Now all is over with us! Did you hear? Tomorrow early she will take us into the thickest part of the forest and leave us there."
"Be quiet, Gretel."
Hansel has a plan.

"Be quiet, Gretel, do not distress yourself, I will soon find a way to help us. " He gets up, puts on his little coat, opens the door below and creeps outside. The moon shines brightly, and the white pebbles in front of the house glitter like real silver pennies.
Gather the white pebbles in front of the house (they glitter like silver pennies).
A pebble in your pocket.
Early in the morning the mother leads you deep into the forest. Go to the middle of the wood.
"Pile up some wood, children, and we will light a fire." Wait by the fire till the moon rises.
🌕 The full moon rises. The pebbles shine like newly-coined silver pieces.
The middle of the wood
Follow the shining pebbles home (press E in the middle of the wood, then walk from pebble to pebble to the cottage).
Not long afterwards they are taken out again, and this time Hansel only has bread to crumble. Look for his crumbs.
A crumb. The birds have had the rest.
🐦 The many thousands of birds that fly about in the woods and fields have picked them all up. You are lost.
A snow-white bird on a bough
On the third morning a beautiful snow-white bird sings on a bough. Listen to it.
🐦 It spreads its wings and flies before you, and you follow it until you reach a little house.
The little house is built of bread and covered with cakes, the windows of clear sugar. Go in.
"Nibble, nibble, gnaw, who is nibbling at my little house?" A very, very old woman comes out, leaning on crutches.

"Oh, you dear children, who has brought you here? Do come in, and stay with me. No harm shall happen to you. " She gives you milk and pancakes with sugar, apples and nuts... (She has red eyes and cannot see far, but she has a keen scent, like the beasts.)
Hansel, in the cage
Hansel is shut in a little stable with a grated door. Speak with him.

"Every morning she cries, 'Hansel, stretch out your finger that I may feel if you will soon be fat.' And I stretch out a little bone instead, and she cannot see, and she wonders why I never grow fat. Gretel, be clever!"
"Creep in, and see if it is properly heated." Be clever, as Gretel was (the great oven).
The witch's chests
Hansel is free! Look in the witch's chests: pearls and precious stones.
The great water: a white duck swimming
Out of the witch's wood: at the great water there is no bridge. Ask the white duck to carry you over.
Find your way home to the woodcutter.
A little cap of red velvet
Once upon a time there was a dear little girl
Little Red-Cap's home is west of Kassel, at the edge of the wood. Go in.
Her mother has a piece of cake and a bottle of wine.

"Come, Little Red-Cap, here is a piece of cake and a bottle of wine; take them to your grandmother, she is ill and weak, and they will do her good. Walk nicely and quietly and do not run off the path , or you may fall and break the bottle. And when you go into her room, don't forget to say 'Good morning'."
"I will take great care."
Little Red-Cap is outside, in her little cap of red velvet. Speak with her.

"My grandmother gave me this cap. It suits me so well I won't wear anything else, so they call me Little Red-Cap! Grandmother lives out in the wood, half a league from the village. Will you walk with me? "
Little Red-Cap's basket
Take the basket: the cake and the wine.
A wolf, by the path
On the path a wolf meets you. Red-Cap does not know what a wicked creature he is. Speak to him.
🐺 "See, Little Red-Cap, how pretty the flowers are about here. Why do you not look round?"
"Grandmother would be pleased with a fresh nosegay." Pick some flowers, a few, close by the path (the wolf is not waiting).
A flower for the nosegay.
Now hurry! Press E at the basket by her home and keep to the path all the way to Grandmother's house (west), before the wolf gets there. (If he wins, start again from the basket.)
Go into Grandmother's house.
Grandmother's bed curtains
"Oh, Grandmother, what big ears you have!" Draw back the bed curtains.
Grandmother is safe. Give her the cake and wine.

Grandmother eats the cake and drinks the wine, and revives. And Little Red-Cap thinks to herself: "As long as I live, I will never by myself leave the path, to run into the wood, when my mother has forbidden me to do so."
The huntsman is passing the house. Speak with him.

"I heard there was a grey wolf about. In the book I found him asleep in the old woman's bed and cut him open, and out they jumped; and we filled his belly with great stones. But you kept to the path, and that is the better ending. In another telling the wolf slid off the roof into the great trough the sausages were boiled in. He'll trouble no one again."
A golden hair from Rapunzel's braid
There were once a man and a woman who had long in vain wished for a child
Their house is in the north-west of the wood, beside a high wall. Go in.
The wife looks down from the little window into the enchantress's garden.
"Look: that bed, planted with the most beautiful rampion. It looks so fresh and green. If I can't have some of it to eat, I shall die. "
Her husband loves her.
"Sooner than let my wife die, I'll bring her some of the rampion myself, let it cost what it will. At twilight I'll clamber over the wall. Will you keep watch with me?"
The enchantress's garden gate
At twilight, climb over the wall into the enchantress's garden and gather the rampion. Don't let her near you.
The years go by. The child is born, and the enchantress takes her and calls her Rapunzel. Wait in the wood by the tower.
🗼 When she is twelve years old, the enchantress shuts her into a tower in the forest, which has neither stairs nor door.
A king's son rides through the forest and hears a song so charming that he stands still and listens.

"Whose voice is that? There is no door in the tower anywhere. I've watched from behind a tree: the old woman calls, and a ladder of gold comes down. If that is the ladder by which one mounts, I too will try my fortune."
The tower with no door
Go to the tower and call: "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, let down your hair."
Rapunzel is frightened at first. Speak gently with her.

"He will love me more than old Dame Gothel does... I will willingly go away with you, but I do not know how to get down. Bring a skein of silk every time you come, and I will weave a ladder with it, and then I will descend, and you will take me on your horse."
"I'll bring silk."
The window, with its hook
Climb back down the braid.
The enchantress finds out, cuts off the braids and casts Rapunzel into a desert. The king's son leaps from the tower, and the thorns blind him. Walk the forest as he did, gathering what you can.
He ate nothing but roots and berries, and did naught but lament and weep.
At length he comes to the desert where Rapunzel lives. Stand still and listen for her voice.

💧 Rapunzel knows him and falls on his neck and weeps. Two of her tears wet his eyes, and they grow clear again, and he can see with them as before. He leads her to his kingdom, where they live a long time afterwards, happy and contented.
A feather from Mother Holle's bed
Once upon a time there was a widow who had two daughters
The widow's house is west of Kassel, by the well. Go in.
The widow is hard on her stepdaughter.

"The ugly lazy one is my own daughter, so I love her better. The other does all the work , and Cinderella of the house she is. Every day she sits by the well in the highway and spins till her fingers bleed."
The good daughter is by the well, spinning.
🩸 The good daughter

"My fingers bled, and I bent over the well to wash the shuttle, and it dropped out of my hand and fell to the bottom. My stepmother says, 'Since you have let the shuttle fall in, you must fetch it out again.' I don't know what to do..."
"Then we'll jump in."
Jump into the well after the shuttle.
The oven, full of bread
You wake in a beautiful meadow where the sun shines. Go to the oven full of bread, and take it out.
The apple tree, heavy with apples
"Oh, shake me, shake me! My apples are all ripe!" Shake the apple tree.
A little house; an old woman peeps out with very large teeth. Go in to Mother Holle.
Mother Holle has work for you.

"What are you afraid of, dear child? Stay with me; if you will do all the work in the house properly, you shall be the better for it. Only you must take care to make my bed well, and shake it thoroughly till the feathers fly, for then there is snow on the earth. I am Mother Holle."
Mother Holle's featherbed
Shake out the featherbed till the feathers fly like snowflakes (three times, done well).
You have grown homesick. Mother Holle leads you to the great gate. Walk through it.
Your stepsister wants gold too.
🖤 The lazy daughter

She throws herself into the well, but in the meadow she lets the bread burn and the apples hang; she will not shake the bed, and when Mother Holle leads her to the gate, a big kettleful of pitch is emptied over her. "That is the reward of your service," says Mother Holle. And the pitch stuck fast to her, and could not be got off as long as she lived.
Half an apple, white and red
Once upon a time in the middle of winter, when the flakes of snow were falling like feathers
The Queen's castle stands north of Kassel. Go in.
The stair to the Queen's chamber
Go up the stair to the Queen's chamber.
The mirror on the wall
"Looking-glass, looking-glass, on the wall, who in this land is the fairest of all?" Ask it.
The Queen's huntsman
The Queen summons a huntsman. Find him outside the castle.
"Where did she run?"
She ran over sharp stones and through thorns, as long as her feet would go, over the seven mountains. Follow her north to the dwarfs' cottage.
Everything in the little cottage is small, but neater and cleaner than can be told. Go in.
Seven little plates, seven little cups, seven little beds. Take a bite and a sip from each, and try the beds, as Snow-White did.
The seven dwarfs come home from the mountains, where they dig and delve for ore. Speak with one.

"Who has been sitting on my chair? Who has been eating off my plate? ... Oh, heavens! What a lovely child! If you will keep our house for us, and cook, make the beds, wash, sew and knit, you can stay with us. But beware of your stepmother: she will soon know you are here. Let no one come in. "
"I'll let no one in."
Pretty laces, bright-coloured
The Queen, painted and dressed like an old pedlar woman, has laces to sell. Pick up the lace she dropped.
🎀 She laced Snow-White so quickly and so tightly that her breath was stopped. The dwarfs cut the lace in two, and she began to breathe a little.
The Queen comes again, disguised as another old woman. Find the comb she left.
🪮 The moment the comb was put in her hair, the poison in it took effect. The dwarfs drew it out, and she came to herself.
A poisoned apple, white and red
The Queen comes a third time, as a peasant's wife, with an apple whose red cheek is poisoned. Find it.
take it (do not eat it!)
A golden goose feather
Briar Rose, asleep
